limits: Single worked dataset (NSFG pregnancy length), so numbers are illustrations, not general findings.
Author concedes the naive Bayesian HA (delta fixed at observed value) is 'a little bit bogus' and overstates evidence.
Chi-square result uses same data for exploration and testing; author advises confirming on another dataset.
Type I/II definitions as printed (Type I: 'accept a hypothesis that is actually false') use confusing wording about which hypothesis is accepted.
Power exercise 7.7 is posed but no power value is computed; exercise answers not given.
Python 2-era code (erf.NormalCdf, thinkstats.com downloads); URLs not fetched.
practices: Choose a p-value threshold alpha (commonly 5%) and call effects with p<alpha significant (7.2).
Lower alpha trades fewer false positives for more false negatives; only a larger sample (or less measurement error) lowers both (7.2).
State whether the test is two-sided or one-sided; define 'the effect' before testing (7.3).
Use separate training and testing data to avoid inflated posteriors (7.5).
Report the likelihood ratio (Bayes factor) so readers can apply their own priors (7.6).
Test a hypothesis that directly reflects the effect (chi-square on categories) rather than variances, which test badly (7.7).
With a negative result, report power: 'if the effect were as large as x, this test would reject the null with probability p' (7.9).
Resample with replacement (random.choice, not random.sample) for the pooled-distribution test (Ex 7.1).

terms.definition: An effect is statistically significant if it is unlikely to occur by chance.
A model of a system based on the assumption that an apparent effect is due to chance.
The probability that an effect could occur by chance.
A test that asks, "What is the chance of an effect as big as the observed effect, positive or negative?"
A test that asks, "What is the chance of an effect as big as the observed effect, and with the same sign?"
A process of hypothesis testing that uses one dataset for exploratory data analysis and another dataset for testing.
A statistic used to measure the deviation of an apparent effect from what is expected by chance.
The ratio of P(E|A) to P(E|B) for two hypotheses A and B, a way to report Bayesian results without depending on priors.
In a chi-square test, the categories the observations are divided into.
The probability that a test will reject the null hypothesis if it is false.
